C4 (Alaska BEAD Subgrantee Execution) — Gate 1 fails: the Alaska-specific trigger (AKBizMag March 18) is outside all windows; the in-window trigger (bbcmag May 6) covers North Dakota only. C5 (GCI/Quintillion FCC Transfer Stack) — Gate 3 fails across multiple layers: FCC.gov returned HTTP 503 throughout the run, preventing confirmation of International Bureau Chief transfer authority from a fetched primary source; NTIA BEAD GTCs PDF (Section 51.C.2.b transfer consent) returned HTTP 403; DoJ NSD Layer 2 has no fetched primary source; DA-26-324A1 public notice PDF was binary-unreadable; the chain cannot be per-layer sourced. C6 (Koniag STARS III) — Gate 1 fails: EINPresswire is a company-issued press release wire service, explicitly excluded by Gate 1; additionally, GSA STARS III page names no individual PM with option exercise authority, so Gate 5 would also be borderline. C7 (BEAD NTIA Net Neutrality Gate) — Gate 5 fails: the compliance gate is exercised by unnamed 'federal program officers,' not a single named individual with binary institutional authority; Arielle Roth is NTIA head but is presented as articulating policy, not as the individual chokepoint executing compliance holds. C8, C9 — Gate 7 fails: both are adjacent to the excluded ANC 8(a) pipeline mechanism (anatomized 2026-05-25). C10 — subsumed into C5 per overlap rule, drops for same Gate 3 reasons. C11 — Gate 1 fails: April 22 trigger is outside both 14-day and 21-day windows. No mechanism survived all seven gates in either window. This is a correct no-target outcome; the bar was not lowered.

Editor’s Note

Cycle summary: Four scouts ran in parallel across facilities, vehicles, capital_sovereignty, and regulatory categories. Eleven candidates were surfaced and merged. The stack-mapper applied the full seven-point anti-confabulation gate and 21-day broadening retry. Recurring infrastructure failures (FCC.gov 503, NTIA BEAD GTCs PDF 403, DoD instruction pages 403) blocked Gate 3 for the strongest candidates (GCI/Quintillion FCC transfer stack, DAF EUL delegation chain). The Koniag STARS III mechanism is the most promising near-miss: the ACT-IAC award was covered only on a company press release wire (EINPresswire) with no independent news publication picking it up by run time — Gate 1 fails on that technicality. If an independent news outlet covers the STARS III option exercise or the Army Contracting Agentic AI Suite before July 1, 2026, that mechanism should resurface in the next run as a high-confidence candidate.

Pattern note for the human: This is the fifth consecutive no-target run (June 2–6). The primary recurring failure mode is Gate 3 (per-layer primary source) when government infrastructure (FCC.gov, DoD instruction portals) returns 503/403 under the Trusted network policy. The secondary failure mode is Gate 5 (diffuse chokepoint) for regulatory bodies that are multi-member commissions. A third failure mode is Gate 1 for mechanisms whose best coverage is press-release wire (EINPresswire, BusinessWire) without independent news pick-up.

No subagent stalls this run. All four scouts and the mapper completed normally. Window was broadened to 21 days as required; still no survivors.
